<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
- Add support for python virtual environments in Lean, allowing overriding of base libraries with py venv directory config value ("python-venv") for local use or job packet var ("sPythonVirtualEnvironment") for cloud.
     - Refactor AddPythonPaths to prepend to path to use for this solution
     - Add static ActivatePythonVirtualEnvironment to prepend the virtual environment libraries to PythonPath, so that they are used.

- Add "venv" virtual environment to foundation image, acts a shell install that gets mounted on later.
- Add Jupyter Kernel for this venv to allow switching to this set of libraries

comments: @jcandan we'd prefer to not make breaking changes to users algorithms; if you could find a way we could install both and optionally use 2.0 we'll install it into the lean-foundation.

Is there any update on this, @jaredbroad ?

Users with tensorflow 1 could use

```
import tensorflow.compat.v1 as tf
tf.disable_v2_behavior()

```
if they want to continue using tensorflow 1 (see https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/migrate for some caveats).
Appreciate if you can prioritise this issue. TF1 is too slow and training timeout after 30min.
Update on this? TF1 is now quite outdated and TF2 has massive usability improvements. Not to mention the TF docs don't reflect TF1 at all anymore, so this could be quite confusing for new users.

Hi Team am getting below error while running LSTM in Quantconnect, Seems like its related to tf2, can anyone help with that.

EXCEPTION:WARNING:tensorflow:OMP_NUM_THREADS is no longer used by the default Keras config. To configure the number of threads, use tf.config.threading APIs.,2020-12-02 13:18:39.993700: I tensorflow/core/platform/cpu_feature_guard.cc:145] This TensorFlow binary is optimized with Intel(R) MKL-DNN to use the following CPU instructions in performance critical operations: SSE4.1 SSE4.2 AVX AVX2 FMA, To enable them in non-MKL-DNN operations, rebuild TensorFlow with the appropriate compiler flags.,2020-12-02 13:18:40.024441: I tensorflow/core/platform/profile_utils/cpu_utils.cc:94] CPU Frequency: 3999980000 Hz, 2020-12-02 13:18:40.024529: I tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/service.cc:168] XLA service 0x7f51ab7ca6f0 initialized for platform Host (this does not guarantee that XLA will be used). Devices:,2020-12-02 13:18:40.024573: I tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/service.cc:176] StreamExecutor device (0): Host, Default Version, 2020-12-02 13:18:40.025017: I tensorflow/c
Hi, I'd like to be able to use tf2 as well. Tf2 opens many more possibilities than tf1.
What is the status of TensorFlow 2.4
None of the new research is based on TF 1.x. This is a huge missed opportunity.
I'm assuming at this point that QC does not want to support traders who want/need to build deep learning models for trading.

I believe the new LEAN CLI can accommodate this. 

It has been a while since I played with machine learning, but is it correct that one can build and train a model, and supply the trained model to be used by a python project without any longer requiring tensor flow libraries?

If so, I think this is just the power offered by CLI.

The CLI supports TensorFlow 2+ for local projects using its [custom libraries](https://www.lean.io/docs/lean-cli/tutorials/custom-libraries) feature. After running `lean library add <project name> tensorflow` you can use the latest version of TensorFlow in local backtests, local research, local optimization and local live trading on the given project.

Using the CLI to transfer locally trained models to the cloud is not possible at the moment.

>       /// <remarks>If a module is already loaded, Python will use its cached version first
 >       /// these modules must be reloaded by reload() from importlib library</remarks>

Not sure we need to worry about supporting this use case? Should always be switch before starting? or maybe research use case 🤔

Yeah little grey area here.

In the use case of launching lean, our implementation calls this before python is initialized so this problem does not apply. But when I was trying to use a unit test to prove the override, when the test assembly loaded it initialized PythonNet and imported pandas somewhere in our python project.

When it got to my unit test and I called this ActivatePythonVirtualEnvironment it worked on TF, since it hadn't been imported yet, but with Pandas it used the already loaded module.
Just thought it may be nice to leave as a remark for anyone who messes around with this. 😁
Would be sweet if we can directly avoid the need of the cache 👍

We don't need it per say, but I noticed in testing that we were adding the same directories more than once. Seemed like a lightweight solution to keep us from  duplicating dirs on our PythonPath on accident.
Could always get the list<strings> on the fly and remove any duplicates before appending/inserting 😁
